originalTitle: News Corp subscriptions fall in Australia as company takes aim at ‘slimy’ AI slop
summary: Chief executive Robert Thomson says ‘crass kleptomaniac’ AI companies are ‘in possession of stolen goods’
content: News Corp has reported a slight slide in digital subscriptions at its Australian mastheads, erasing recent gains, among otherwise robust financials at the Rupert Murdoch-backed global conglomerate. Digital subscribers at News Corp Australia – a division that includes the Australian, the Daily Telegraph and the Herald Sun, among others – fell from 1,166,000 to 1,162,000 during the financial year, according to the company’s internal data published in its full year results on Thursday morning. The figures represent a reversal in momentum. The Australian division has grown digital subscriptions in recent years, as it transitions away from its traditional newspaper base. Sign up for the Breaking News Australia email News Corp’s broader news media unit, which includes the Sun and the Times in London and the New York Post, recorded mixed results, with advertising revenue still under pressure, falling 2% during the year to 30 June. The news media division also recorded costs linked to the launch of News Corp’s latest newspaper, the California Post, which is the Los Angeles outpost of the New York Post and edited by Australian News Corp veteran Nick Papps. The News Corp chief executive, Robert Thomson, used the release of the company’s financial results to hit out at AI models that “pilfer and profit from our work”, as media companies around the world seek compensation for the use of their content. “Without our journalists, our authors, our data, our brands and our professional expertise, users would be drowning in a slimy sea of AI slop,” Thomson said. “We will pursue those pilferers and companies that are clients of these crass kleptomaniacs should know they are patently in possession of stolen goods.” News Corp has commercial agreements in place with OpenAI and Meta. The comments come amid contested plans by the Albanese government to expand its news bargaining incentive, which would require tech giants to compensate media outlets for the news on their platforms, either through making commercial deals or paying a higher levy.
chineseTitle: 新闻集团在澳大利亚的订阅量下降，因为该公司瞄准了“粘糊糊”的 AI 领域
chineseSummary: 首席执行官罗伯特·汤姆森 (Robert Thomson) 表示，人工智能公司是“严重的盗窃狂”，“拥有赃物”
chineseContent: 新闻集团报告称，其澳大利亚报头的数字订阅量略有下滑，抹去了近期的涨幅，而鲁珀特·默多克支持的全球企业集团的财务状况却强劲。澳大利亚新闻集团（包括《澳大利亚人报》、《每日电讯报》和《先驱太阳报》等）的数字订户在本财年从 1,166,000 人下降至 1,162,000 人，该公司周四上午在其全年业绩中发布的内部数据显示。这些数字代表了势头的逆转。近年来，随着其从传统报纸基地转型，澳大利亚分部的数字订阅量不断增长。新闻集团旗下更广泛的新闻媒体部门，包括伦敦的《太阳报》、《泰晤士报》和《纽约邮报》，业绩好坏参半，广告收入仍面临压力，截至 6 月 30 日的一年内下降了 2%。新闻媒体部门还记录了与新闻集团最新报纸《加州邮报》发行相关的成本，该报纸是《纽约邮报》在洛杉矶的前哨站，由澳大利亚新闻集团资深人士尼克·帕普斯编辑。新闻集团首席执行官罗伯特·汤姆森 (Robert Thomson) 利用公司财务业绩的发布，猛烈抨击人工智能模型“窃取我们的工作并从中获利”，因为世界各地的媒体公司都在寻求对其内容的使用进行补偿。汤姆森说：“如果没有我们的记者、作者、数据、品牌和专业知识，用户将淹没在人工智能泥浆的泥泞海洋中。” “我们将追捕那些小偷，而这些粗鲁的盗窃狂的客户公司应该知道他们显然拥有赃物。”新闻集团与 OpenAI 和 Meta 签订了商业协议。通讯
whyItMatters: 这条信息属于全球新闻信号，适合用于观察外部环境、政策变化、地缘风险和市场情绪。
